label: Management system standards
summary: Certifiable management systems (ISO/IEC 27001, ISO 22301, ISO/IEC 42001, ISO 45001). The certification body fixes audit time from scope, headcount, sites and complexity before Stage 1, and the auditor reads the scope, interested parties and Statement of Applicability first.

requires_org.reason: Sites are the unit of audit planning and multi-site sampling.
The scope names the systems and interfaces inside the boundary.
Top management must own the scope and the policy.

source.ref: Certification-body quote forms and service procedures: Stage 1, Stage 2, 3-year certificate, annual surveillance

fields.label: Goal
fields.note: Decides how strict the gate is. A certificate needs a named body and audit dates; alignment does not.

fields.label: Certification body
fields.note: The accredited body that will audit. It asks for the scope data below in its application, so name it early.

fields.label: Certificate type
fields.note: Transfers and recertifications need the previous certificate and its audit reports.

fields.label: Current certificate
fields.note: Certificate number and expiry. The body checks the previous scope and open nonconformities.

fields.label: Stage 1 target
fields.note: Stage 1 is the documentation and readiness review. Bodies check that internal audit and management review are planned before it.

fields.label: Stage 2 target
fields.note: Stage 2 is the implementation audit. Nonconformities are normally closed within about six weeks before the decision.

source.ref: Clauses 4.1 and 4.2 of each standard (issues, interested parties and their requirements), as restated in certification-body gap guides

fields.label: Issues
fields.note: Internal and external issues that affect the management system (market, regulation, technology, ownership). The auditor checks they were thought about, not their length.

fields.label: Interested parties
fields.note: Who has requirements of the system and what they are. Listing parties without their requirements is the commonest gap.

fields.label: Obligations reviewed
fields.note: Confirms the legal, regulatory and contractual requirements in the organisation profile were reviewed for this system.

fields.label: Climate change

source.ref: ISO Amendment 1:2024 adds a climate-change question to clause 4.1 (reported by certification bodies; not read in the standard text)

fields.note: Since the 2024 amendment, auditors ask whether climate change is a relevant issue and expect the decision recorded.

source.ref: Clause 4.3 (boundaries, activities, products, locations, interfaces and dependencies; documented; exclusions justified) and the certification body's sizing data

fields.label: Scope statement
fields.note: The sentence printed on the certificate. Say what is covered, where, and for whom. Too narrow a scope drawn for one customer is the commonest reason to redraw it later.

fields.label: Scope kind
fields.note: The shape of the boundary.

fields.label: Entities
fields.note: Legal entities inside the scope, picked from the organisation profile.

fields.label: Sites
fields.note: Sites inside the scope. The body spreads audit days across sites by relevance and risk; multi-site sampling needs a central function.

fields.label: Units
fields.note: Departments inside the scope.

fields.label: Systems
fields.note: Systems and services inside the boundary. Include the interfaces to systems outside it.

fields.label: Staff in scope
fields.note: People inside the scope including contractors and freelancers. ISO/IEC 27006-1 counts non-employees for audit time.

fields.label: Shift pattern
fields.note: Shifts and staff per shift when work runs round the clock. Bodies add audit time for shifts.

fields.label: Outsourced
fields.note: Outsourced processes and providers inside the scope. An outsourced process stays in scope; its provider's controls are covered by contract or evidence.

fields.label: Interfaces
fields.note: Dependencies on organisations or systems outside the boundary (clause 4.3). Auditors ask what happens at each interface.

fields.label: Exclusions
fields.note: Anything inside the organisation left out, each with the reason. An unjustified exclusion is a finding. Leave empty if nothing is excluded.

fields.label: Business type

source.ref: NSAI ISO 27001 quote form, complexity categories 1 to 3 (authoritative for that body only, others differ)

fields.note: Feeds the body's audit-time calculation. Bodies word these categories differently.

fields.label: Process type
fields.note: How varied the work in scope is. Same use as above.

fields.label: System maturity
fields.note: How far a management system already exists. Same use as above.

fields.label: Services in scope

source.ref: ISO 22301 clause 4.3: products and services in scope, locations, exclusions; BIA inputs

fields.note: Products and services the continuity system protects, with the longest outage the business can tolerate.

fields.label: AI role

source.ref: ISO/IEC 42001 clause 4.1 and ISO/IEC 22989 roles, as explained by certification and audit firms

fields.note: The organisation's role towards its AI systems decides which controls matter. One organisation can hold several roles.

fields.label: AI systems
fields.note: Every AI system in scope, including bought and embedded AI. Inventories that miss third-party AI are the usual gap.

fields.label: Workers in scope

source.ref: ISO 45001 clauses 4.1 to 4.3: workers and other persons under the organisation's control; scope by workplace and activity

fields.note: Paid or unpaid people doing work under the organisation's control, including contractors on site.

fields.label: Hazardous work
fields.note: Main hazards and hazardous activities, shutdown periods and contractors on site. The body schedules Stage 2 around them.

source.ref: Clauses 6.1.2 and 6.1.3 (risk criteria, risk treatment, Statement of Applicability); ISO 22301 BIA; ISO 42001 clause 6.1.4 impact assessment; ISO 45001 hazards and consultation

fields.label: Risk criteria
fields.note: Acceptance and assessment criteria must exist before risks are assessed, or results are not comparable.

fields.label: Risk owners named
fields.note: Risk owners approve the treatment plan and accept residual risk.

fields.label: SoA status
fields.note: The Statement of Applicability lists necessary controls, why, whether implemented and why others are excluded. The auditor uses it as the central document. Not started is allowed at onboarding.

fields.label: SoA owner
fields.note: Who keeps the SoA current.

fields.label: BIA status
fields.note: The business impact analysis fixes impact criteria, time frames and prioritised activities. Auditors expect it linked to the risk assessment.

fields.label: Impact process
fields.note: ISO 42001 requires a process to assess effects of AI systems on people and society, with results documented.

fields.label: Hazard method
fields.note: How hazards and risks are identified and assessed.

fields.label: Worker consultation
fields.note: How workers take part (committee, representatives). Auditors ask for evidence that they did.

source.ref: Clause 5.3 (top management assigns and communicates roles) and clause 5 (leadership, policy)

fields.label: Top management
fields.note: The member of top management who owns the system and approves scope, policy and risk acceptance.

fields.label: System manager
fields.note: Runs the system day to day (ISMS, BCM, AI or OH&S manager). No role title is mandated; someone must be named.

fields.label: Policy status
fields.note: The top-level policy of the system. Bodies expect it approved before Stage 1.

source.ref: Certification-body procedure: Stage 1 checks that internal audit and management review are planned and performed before Stage 2

fields.label: Internal audit date
fields.note: Planned date of the first internal audit. It must happen before Stage 2.

fields.label: Management review
fields.note: Planned date of the first management review. Same rule.

fields.label: Internal auditor
fields.note: Who audits. They should not audit what they run.

gate.label: Scope names at least one site
gate.hint: Pick the sites inside the boundary.

gate.label: Internal audit is planned before Stage 2
gate.hint: Bodies check that an internal audit has been done before Stage 2.

gate.label: Management review is planned before Stage 2
gate.hint: Same rule for the management review.

gate.label: Stage 1 is planned before Stage 2
gate.hint: Stage 1 findings are fixed before Stage 2.

gate.label: Top management and system manager are different people
gate.hint: Top management owns; the manager runs.
